entries.name:
guideline: Navigation.

In the highlight selection style fo

fields.before: List views display content in a structured, scrollable list. They support sorting, organizing, and selecting multiple items at once.
fields.after:
Navigation.

In the highlight selection style for touch interactions, tapping anywhere on the item will navigate to its contents. For mouse-based interactions, double-clicking anywhere on the item or single-clicking the navigation icon will do the same. In the checkbox selection style, clicking or tapping the label area or navigation icon of a list view item will navigate to its contents.

entries.name:
guideline: Selection.

Single-clicking or tapping anywhere

fields.before: A list view is a versatile component and can contain many items depending on the use case. These items can be icons, thumbnails, avatars, checkboxes, drag handles, action buttons, and more.
fields.after:
Selection.

Single-clicking or tapping anywhere on a list view item will select the item, except the label in checkbox selection style. For checkbox selection style, clicking the label will navigate to the item.

entries.name:
guideline: Touch navigation and selection.

In touch experi

fields.before: By default a list view is not quiet. If true, the list view uses a quiet visual style meaning there is no background or borders to the component.
fields.after:
Touch navigation and selection.

In touch experiences, the list view default is navigation only with the highlight selection style. Users enter a selection mode by a touch and hold gesture on any list view item. Selection mode in touch uses the checkbox selection style and suppresses navigation. Users can exit selection mode by pressing the Escape key or deselecting all items.

entries.name:
guideline: Drag and drop.

List view items can be dragged a

fields.before: The selection mode defines how many items can be selected at once. A list view can use single selection, multiple selection, or none.
fields.after:
Drag and drop.

List view items can be dragged and dropped to reorder or restructure the list. Multiple items can be dragged at a time and shifted from one level of hierarchy to another. List views can also accept dropped items from outside the component, to modify the list. Keyboard-based drag and drop When using this option for a list view, the drag icon receives keyboard focus in order to allow for a keyboard-based drag and drop interaction. Touch-based drag and drop The drag and drop interaction is initiated by a touch and hold gesture, followed by drag gesture. If a user performs a touch and hold gesture without dragging, the list view enters a selection mode.

entries.name:
guideline: Text overflow.

A list view item's label or desc

fields.before: In the highlight selection style for touch interactions, tapping anywhere on the item will navigate to its contents. For mouse-based interactions, double-clicking anywhere on the item or single-clicking the navigation icon will do the same.
fields.after:
Text overflow.

A list view item's label or description will truncate if the text is longer than the available horizontal space. Display the full label or description text in a tooltip on hover and focus states.

fields.before: In the checkbox selection style, clicking or tapping the label area or navigation icon of a list view item will navigate to its contents.
fields.after:

entries.name:
guideline: When to use a List view vs. Tree view.

List vie

fields.before: Single-clicking or tapping anywhere on a list view item will select the item, except the label in checkbox selection style. For checkbox selection style, clicking the label will navigate to the item.
fields.after:
When to use a List view vs. Tree view.

List views work best for flat collections of items that share the same hierarchy level. Tree views are ideal for displaying nested or hierarchical relationships.

before.description: Icon indicating a list view item navigates to a new context.

after.name: container
after.description: The list view: border, background, corner radius and minimum width. It is the root.

after.name: drill-in-chevron
after.description: Non-interactive chevron that shows an item navigates to another level (Figma Navigation indicator). The whole item is the target.

after.name: focus-indicator
after.description: Outline drawn around the focused item.

after.name: section-header
after.description: Heading above a group of rows.

fields.before: Action buttons or action menu available for a list view item.
fields.after: Row of action buttons at the end of an item; hosts the actions slot.

fields.before: A single row within the list view.
fields.after: A single row within the list view; repeated once per entry of items. Its position in the list (first, middle, last, only) is derived from the entry order.

after.name: actions
after.description: Actions at the end of an item.

after.name: default
after.description: The rows. Each entry of the items option is drawn as one copy of the list-item part.

fields.after: Figma S2 Web list view page and React Spectrum S2 ListView. container added as the root (border, background, radius, minimum width). Decision A65 D2a: an item's position in the list is derived from entry order, so the authored itemRounding entry option is deleted; the component data has no field for a derived position (see the report). Decision A71 D8 a2: trailing-icon renamed drill-in-chevron, non-interactive. drag-handle, section-header and focus-indicator (keyboard-focus state added) added. Decision A68 D5a: list-view keeps its own records; stack-item holds the shared row chrome. actions is a slot host (accepts action-button, up to 3).
